claims.text: MLIPs trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations of a target HEA will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to EAM references.
Improved phase-space overlap from MLIP references will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch near melting.
The proposed method is applicable to near-equiatomic HEAs containing 4–6 principal elements.
The proposed temperature range is 0.8–1.2 times the melting temperature.
MLIPs trained on both phases can represent the local atomic environments and chemical disorder found in HEA solids and liquids.
EAM models are generally parametrized for simpler and often crystalline environments and consequently represent HEA solid and liquid disorder less effectively.
Training on diverse ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations from both phases gives MLIPs substantially greater overlap with the ab initio target distribution than EAM models.
Reduced configurational mismatch along the integration path produces more accurate and less biased free-energy estimates.
MLIP references will reduce systematic free-energy error relative to ab initio by at least a factor of two compared with EAM references.
The improvement from MLIP references will be especially large in the liquid phase.
EAM fails to capture chemical disorder in the liquid phase.
The improved overlap can be detected through overlap metrics or reduced variance of the thermodynamic-integration estimator.
The EAM references used in TOR-TILD have poor overlap with ab initio liquid configurations in multicomponent HEAs.
Poor EAM–ab initio liquid overlap in TOR-TILD causes significant path mismatch and free-energy error.
The proposed method may not apply to strongly segregating or ordering compositions or to temperatures far from melting when relevant MLIP training data are sparse.
MLIPs may fail to represent rare configurations or long-range effects absent from their training data.
